### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **69** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**55** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 48 pages)`
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ff6056b47f5007d6a9ff53b88cb44ca29e40e250` — the merge of head `3cabcf9038f97b8208e57b6a1711cbc91683d6d1` into base `4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ff6056b47f5007d6a9ff53b88cb44ca29e40e250 && git checkout ff6056b47f5007d6a9ff53b88cb44ca29e40e250
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4 3cabcf9038f97b8208e57b6a1711cbc91683d6d1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4 && git merge --no-ff 3cabcf9038f97b8208e57b6a1711cbc91683d6d1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b06a54ad664abc832cdb56b66bfd42a34efaaf4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `82e68cec23420fd9aa3a66e17f0f87a1e3582467`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts + packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/user-device.object.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/notifications.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (read for the red gate), packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts and packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts (read for the markers that stay), packages/runtime/src/api-exposure.ts and packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts (read for the exposure claim), packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts (read for the retry claim)

Reviewed against: card #29068 (body, seat 5 ruling 6571089853, the two claims, dev report 6590239185 stamped 2026-11-02T22:36Z), PR #29628 body and 42-file diff, the #29067 contract on `main` (`push-device.zod.ts` rules a/b/c, `protocol.zod.ts` RegisterDevice*/UnregisterDevice*, the `INotificationService` device members, `.changeset/29067-push-device-registry-spec.md`), and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (service-messaging, runtime, client, tests, census, generated bundles and docs) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` on the declaration face, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and is named below only where a `hits` hunk makes a claim about it.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Two served routes, `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices` and `DELETE /api/v1/notifications/devices/:deviceId`** — right. Both rows sit in `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` with `handler` names that are also in the registration's `methods` array, `public: false`, `authRequired: true` inherited, `requestSchema: 'RegisterDeviceRequestSchema'` bound on the POST row, no request schema on the DELETE row (the id is a path segment; `UnregisterDeviceRequestSchema` is body-shaped and would have demanded a violating-body case for a route with no body), and `responseSchema` on both. The `methods` entries are part of the same table the ruling names; they ride with hunk 1 and are inside the allowance.
2. **The PLANNED markers come off exactly the schemas now served** — right. Five descriptions lose the marker: the four `RegisterDevice*` / `UnregisterDevice*` schemas and `UserDeviceSchema`; the three "marker comes off when #29068…" comments go with them. `push-delivery.zod.ts` (`[PLANNED — not yet served]`) and `push-config.zod.ts` (`[PLANNED — not yet read]`) keep theirs: nothing in this PR serves a push or reads the transport config, and those belong to #29041. The `Spec property liveness` check-run is green on the head. The spec test pins (`register-device-request.test.ts`, `push-device.test.ts`, the `plugin-rest-api.test.ts` 3→5 route count) are the forced edits of those hunks and say the true thing.
3. **`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` gains `sys_user_device` under `service-messaging`** — right: that is the package that registers and provisions it (`messaging-service-plugin.ts` adds `UserDevice` to both the `objects` list and `provisionSystemTables`), and `bundle-ownership.test.ts`, the i18n extract config and the four generated bundles follow it.
4. **`contracts/notification-service.ts` comment-only edit** — outside the three named hunks, and accepted: no member, type or shape moves; the paragraph it replaces ("no provider implements them and no route calls them yet") would be false on this head. A comment that contradicts the tree is worse than a fourth prose hunk. Named as a deviation, not a breach.
5. **Served shapes match the spec** — right. The POST body is `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.safeParse(body ?? {})` on the catalog row's own schema (unknown keys such as a body `userId` are stripped, pinned by `notifications-devices.test.ts`); the answer is `{ deviceId, success }` with the server-minted `randomUUID()` when the request carried none; DELETE answers `{ success: true }`. Vendor derives `ios→apns`, `android→fcm`; a `web` registration without `vendor` is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` at field `vendor`, never stored with a guess — exactly the contract's third bullet.
6. **Rule (a), a device belongs to a user** — right. `tenancy: { enabled: false }`, no `organization_id`, identity index `(user_id, device_id)`; the census JSON and the CLI ownership inventory both record it as out of tenancy reach with the reason. For a multi-org user this means one row per app install regardless of which organization the session is in, which is what rule (a) asks. An organization admin has no door to another member's devices: no `GET /devices` route exists (the card says none), `listDevices(userId)` is service-only, and the data API is closed (point 8). Right by the card; #29041's push channel will read `listDevices` as the system.
7. **Rule (b), one live row per token, the first user's row removed** — right. `registerOnce` reads the token's holder, deletes that row when it is not the row being refreshed (another user's device, or this user's stale device id), then updates or inserts; `(token)` carries a `unique: 'global'` index so a second holder can never be stored. Pinned by the integration test (`holders` of `tok-shared` is one row, Alice's `alice-phone` gone, her tablet kept) and the dogfood `[takeover]` case on the real stack.
8. **The data API is closed, and no other door opens `sys_user_device`** — right. `enable.apiEnabled: false, apiMethods: []` is the credential-table posture (`sys-connector-credential.object.ts`); `canServeApiOperation` judges `apiEnabled === false` FIRST for every operation, so the REST data door answers `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` for every verb to every principal, an organization or platform admin included (the admin-bypass concern the #29443 memory records applies to an `apiEnabled` object; it does not reach this one). Dogfood `[data-api]` pins list/read/create/patch/delete for a member. `searchable: false` keeps it out of `/search`; `trackHistory: false` keeps it out of the history table; export rides the same `enforceApiAccess` gate as the CRUD routes; the engine emits no `data.record.*` events on `main` (the only producer is service-knowledge), so realtime relays nothing; the MCP bridge reads the same exposure gate. What remains reachable is the object's metadata document under `/meta` (schema, not rows), the same as every credential table.
9. **Rule (c)** — right, see ④.
10. **Anonymous floor first** — right. `handleNotificationRequest` reads `context.executionContext.userId` and answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` before the body is read and before the slot is resolved; the devices branch sits after that floor and after `isServiceServeable`, and probes its own member (501 for an inbox-only provider; served for a registry-only provider), ahead of the `listInbox` probe. The dispatcher plugin mounts both faces plus the other verbs refusal-only on the standalone server, so every verb on the two paths reaches the floor (pinned 15→25 in `dispatcher-plugin.routes.test.ts`).
11. **Client methods and the ledger** — right. `notifications.registerDevice(request)` → `POST {route}/devices`, `unregisterDevice(deviceId)` → `DELETE {route}/devices/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`; the two `sdk` rows name `notifications.registerDevice` / `notifications.unregisterDevice`; eight `server-only` refusal rows; the census comment 116→126 is tool-written.
12. **New exports** — `UserDevice` and `USER_DEVICE_OBJECT` from `@objectstack/service-messaging`, the four device members on `MessagingService` — a widening, named in the changeset.
13. **`Metadata-protocol: none`** — right. Nothing an author writes gains or loses a key, value or type; route rows and `.describe()` text are catalog and prose, not authored metadata. The `Spec property liveness` run is green and `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is untouched (seat 5 freeze, #25467).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29068-push-device-registry.md`: `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/spec` all **`patch`**, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations in both the changeset and the PR body. **Correct**, and the delta's "minor ×3" was the wrong order: AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3 says the level follows the kind alone — a kind takes at least `minor`, **`none` takes `patch`**, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". #29067 took `minor` because it was `Metadata-protocol: added` (new schemas an author could write); this slice adds none. The `Check Changeset` run is green. New served routes and client methods are a widening, so the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is the right face; this record is the review that line owes.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions (dev report 6590239185):

1. **Cross-node token race** — **A, keep**: unique index on `token` plus one retry on a unique violation, beside the in-process per-token chain. Judged against the code: a losing writer's insert or update is refused by the database, `isUniqueViolationError` recognises SQLSTATE 23505, MySQL 1062 and the SQLite message through `cause`, and the second attempt re-reads the winner's row and moves the token from it, which is what the loser asked for. The integration test's three-way `Promise.all` exercises the in-process chain; the cross-node leg rests on the index (pinned by the direct insert being refused). A distributed lock would add an infrastructure dependency the database already supplies. Two residuals, neither blocking, in ④ should-fix 1 and 2.
2. **`user_id` lookup `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`** — **A, keep**. A device row without a user can address no inbox and no push; `set_null` would leave orphan tokens that `invalidateDeviceToken` could still disable but nothing could ever deliver to. Precedent in the same package: `notification-preference.object.ts` cascades on its user lookup and says the default is load-bearing.
3. **Malformed percent-escape in `:deviceId`** — **A, keep, 404**. The segment is decoded as the self-hosted router decodes a parameter, and an escape that does not decode is passed raw (the `/meta` and `automation-hooks` precedent, cited in the code); a raw segment names no device this caller holds, so the owner check is the single answer and a 400 would create a second one that distinguishes "malformed" from "not yours". Pinned in `notifications-devices.test.ts`. The dispatcher mount re-encodes `req.params.deviceId` (Hono hands params decoded) so an id carrying `/` or `%` survives the round trip; the client encodes with `encodeURIComponent`.

Deviations (dev report):

- **Changesets all `patch`** — right, see ②.
- **`contracts/notification-service.ts` comment-only edit** — accepted, see ① 4.
- **`methods` array entries ride with hunk 1** — inside the allowance, see ① 1.
- **Spec test pins flipped** — forced edits of the allowed hunks, see ① 2.
- **`titleFormat` dropped after #29499** — right; `nameField: 'name'` only.

Gate verdicts on the head (the check-runs ARE the verdicts), read at the time of writing: **`Lint · docs & code guards` FAILURE** (`check:error-code-provenance`, ④ must-fix 1), **`Test Core (2/8)` FAILURE** (`@objectstack/spec test:repo`, `platform-object-names.test.ts:171`, ④ must-fix 2), and `Lint & Repo Gates` FAILURE as the lane aggregate of the first. Green: `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the route-ledger, tenant-audit and platform-object-tenancy census gates live here), `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core` shards 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, every `Test UI` shard. Every check-run on the head had completed when this record was written; the three failures are the only non-green conclusions apart from the opt-in and schedule-gated skips.

Same-seat serial overlap with **PR #29575 (#29443, `sys_personal_view`)**: five files are touched by both — `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` (totals 91→92 here, and again there), `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` and `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` (the 255→260 figures and the "Measured on … at …" line), `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts` (a row each) and `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (different package arrays, probably clean). The census files WILL conflict textually: whichever lands second re-merges `main` and re-runs `node scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.mjs --write` and `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` on the merge, then re-pushes. This PR already needs a re-push (④ must-fix 1), so it should merge `main` once more at that point and regenerate if #29575 has landed.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts`** (the two rows) — judged against seat 5 ruling 6571089853 and the first consumer, `request-schema-gate.conformance.test.ts`, which walks every row with a `requestSchema` against the live dispatcher and demands a violating-body case: the case is there (`POST /api/v1/notifications/devices`, five violating bodies, a `registerDevice` spy). The row and its handler land together, as the ruling requires. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** and **`packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts`** (markers off) — judged against the ruling the markers encode ("a served route and a PLANNED marker cannot both be true") and the first consumers: `notifications.ts` parses `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` and answers `RegisterDeviceResponseSchema`'s shape; `toUserDevice` in `device-registry.ts` produces `UserDeviceSchema`'s shape (`invalidatedAt` present exactly while `enabled` is false, `lastSeenAt` from `last_seen_at`, newest-first with never-seen last). Rule (c) at the consumer: `invalidate(token)` keeps the row and writes `enabled: false, invalidated_at: now`; every registration writes `enabled: true, invalidated_at: null, last_seen_at: now`, so the next registration of the same device re-enables it and clears the time — pinned by the integration test (`revived.id === dead.id`, `invalidated_at` null, `relisted` has no `invalidatedAt`) and dogfood `[invalidate]`. The `push-device.zod.ts` docblock now says service-messaging owns the table "while no push channel plugin exists", which is the card's stated fallback. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts`** (comment) — judged against the implementation it now names: `MessagingService.registerDevice/unregisterDevice/listDevices/invalidateDeviceToken` delegate to `DeviceRegistry` with the contract's signatures (`userId` from the session, never a body member — pinned by the "a body userId is not read" case and ablation A5). Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`** — judged against its consumers (bundle ownership, i18n extract, the tenancy census): all three carry the object. Holds.

Trying to break the design:

- Another user's device: `unregister` keys the read `where: { user_id, device_id }` and deletes only the id that read returned, so a non-owner gets `NOT_FOUND` and nothing moves (ablation A1, dogfood `[owner]`). Register binds `userId` from the session (A5). Refresh addresses `(user_id, device_id)` of the caller. The only row of another user a call touches is the token's holder, and the spec says it must go. No path found.
- `web` platform with `vendor` omitted is refused before the lock is taken; nothing is written (pinned).
- A registration with a `deviceId` this user holds and a token one of this user's OTHER devices holds removes the stale row and refreshes the named one — the spec's no-`deviceId` sentence speaks to the storage-cleared case; with a `deviceId` present this is the only reading that keeps one live row per token, and the test names it.

**Must-fix (FAIL):**

1. **The head's `Lint · docs & code guards` lane is red: `check:error-code-provenance` fails** — "`@objectstack/service-messaging` stamps `'NOT_FOUND'` (assign) at `packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.ts:90` — not listed under its own owner key". The code is right (the #29067 contract pins `code: 'NOT_FOUND'` by name, and the ledger's own grandfather entry keeps `NOT_FOUND` on the wire as a synonym of `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` "until it has a measured victim"), so the fix is the ledger row, not a different code: add `'NOT_FOUND'` under the `'@objectstack/service-messaging'` owner key in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, with the comment the gate asks for recording the wire path (`DeviceRegistry.unregister` → `deviceNotFoundError()` → `DELETE /api/v1/notifications/devices/:deviceId` answers 404 through `resolveThrownHttpError`; reachability pinned by dogfood `[owner]` and `[takeover]`). **This record authorises that one line and its comment as a fourth `packages/spec/**` hunk**, nothing else in that file; a `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` entry is the wrong instrument (that is for a door in another package naming the vocabulary, and here the stamping package is the owner). Rerun `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:error-code-provenance` before pushing: it is one of the artifact-roster families `dispatch-gates` scores `silent` for every card (the #14930 precedent its docblock records), so "121 derived, all exit 0" could not have seen it, and the report's claim is true of the derived set and blind to this one. Then regenerate spec artifacts if the ledger drives any, merge `main` once more (③, #29575) and re-push; the record on the new head is a re-read of the ledger hunk and the check-runs, nothing else moves.

2. **The head's `Test Core (2/8)` shard is red: `@objectstack/spec test:repo` fails at `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts:171`** — the pin "no longer resolves the retired sys_notification_subscription" holds `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['service-messaging']` equal to the six objects before this card, and the roster line (spec hunk 3) made it seven. The roster line is right; the pin is the forced test edit it owes: add `'sys_user_device'` to that `toEqual` list (alphabetical position, after `'sys_notification_template'`), the same class of edit as the three spec test pins the report already names. **This record authorises that one-line test edit as part of hunk 3.** Why the dev's "spec 23698 passed / 1 todo" did not see it: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` runs `vitest --project local`; this pin lives in `--project repo` (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo`), which CI's Test Core shard runs. Run `test:repo` before pushing. #29575 adds `sys_personal_view` to a different array of the same constant; if its pin lives in the same file, the second to land re-reads this test after the merge.

**Should-fix (not blocking):**

1. **The register write is not atomic.** `registerOnce` deletes the previous holder, then inserts or updates in a second statement. A non-unique failure between the two (the engine down, a validation refusal on the new row) leaves the token with no holder: the phone is silently unregistered until the client registers again. Acceptable for M1 (the client re-registers on every launch per the contract's `lastSeenAt` story), but record it in the module docblock's "three layers" section as the accepted gap, and take it to a transaction when the engine offers one for this path.
2. **`REGISTER_ATTEMPTS = 2`.** A third concurrent cross-node writer of the same token can make the retry lose too, and the caller then sees the raw unique violation (409 `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`) for a request that is well-formed. One more attempt, or a one-line note in the docblock that the 409 is the deliberate ceiling, would do; a client retrying 409 converges.
3. **Token length is bounded by storage, not by the declared contract.** `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.token` is `z.string()` while `sys_user_device.token` is `maxLength: 512` (the comment prices APNs 64 hex and FCM about 160). An over-long token is refused by the engine's `record-validator` (400 with `maxLength`/`actual`), so no 500, but the refusal is not the one the catalog's `requestSchema` promises. Follow-up on the spec slice (#29041 or a spec card), as a `.max(512)` is a narrowing and not this PR's to make.
4. **`PATCH /notifications/devices/:deviceId` and friends answer 404 "or 501 with no notification service"** — the ledger notes say so and the domain does that; the inbox rows' notes say "with no inbox". Harmonising the two sentence families is cosmetic; leave it unless the ledger census gate ever reads the note text.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-eqmkj9`
